lines.text: Agents need tests. Evals are tests for agents.
I turn real conversations into a dataset of cases.
Every case is scored: is it right, is it grounded, did it call the right tool?
Then I run the same cases on different models and prompts.
And with different sets of tools.
A prompt change breaks something? The evals catch it before users do.
In production, LangSmith keeps scoring real traffic.
The cheapest model that passes wins.
If you don't measure it, you can't improve it.
